newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac warns France against return to socialism.
newsitem.headline: Chirac warns France against return to socialism.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Tuesday he had understood the message of voters who rejected his centre-right government in the first round of a parliamentary election but warned against a return to socialism.
In a short, dramatic television broadcast, Chirac said: "Let us take care not to compromise everything at the moment when we are reaping the first fruits of our efforts."
"Do you really want to put the socialist ideas of yesteryear back in the saddle?," he asked.

Chirac paid tribute to fellow Gaullist Prime Minister Alain Juppe, who announced on Monday he would resign whatever the outcome of next Sunday's decisive runoff ballot after the left-wing opposition outpolled the centre-right by more than four points on last Sunday's first round.

The president called for a modern, decentralised government reconciling economic freedom with social solidarity and gave no hint of which conservative politician he would choose to succeed Juppe if the right won the wide open runoff.

"I hope the majority which you will choose does not take the risk of weakening European integration," he said, after pledging tax cuts to quicken growth and overcome France's record 12.8 percent unemployment.
"We must reconcile liberty, which is the oxygen of economic health, with solidarity, solidarity between generations and protection for those who are the most weak," he said.

"The strong growth which is today within our reach, will benefit everyone. And for there to be strong growth, which is naturally the best way to create jobs, we must lower taxes and charges to the level of other European countries," he said.
